correctness.rationale: For the order \(L\prec H\), iteration gives \(a_r/b_r\le\kappa^r\). Min-max yields \(\sigma_{n-1}\ge b_r\) and \(\sigma_n\le a_r\), so the least singular line is simple and converges uniformly to \(L\). Fixed-time spectral projections are uniformly continuous, hence so is the lifted line. In graph coordinates \(\operatorname{Hom}(L,H)\), the real backward graph-transform derivative is bounded by \(a_r/b_r\); a thin complex strip preserves an invariant contracting graph ball. Fixed-center holomorphic iterates converge uniformly in a single projective chart, giving a holomorphic line extension. The Stein line normalization is ambient-rank independent, after which the Diophantine Fourier lemma solves both scalar equations. The cited arbitrary-rank obstruction and existence results give the criterion; the coset and carried simplicity are then rederived directly by comparing any carried eigensection with the constructed one and using recurrence plus Fourier characters of the torus translation. Reverse domination follows from the inverse cocycle. No finite experiment or unproved asymptotic substitution is used.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 source explicitly restricts its automatic analytic discharge and exact criterion to rank two and states that no higher-rank analogue is asserted. Full-text comparison with the source and with the arbitrary-dimensional domination theorem of Bochi–Gourmelon, plus targeted semantic searches and comparison with Duarte–Klein, found no statement implying the exact higher-rank line-resolved Chern–winding criterion. The principal residual risk is unindexed folklore on analytic regularity of dominated invariant line bundles; that could cover the graph-transform regularity lemma, but no located source combines it with the measurable-eigensection criterion.
residual_risks: A general analytic graph-transform theorem for dominated invariant subbundles may make the holomorphic-extension lemma folklore or an immediate specialization even though no such source was located under the searched terminology.

Duarte–Klein was compared at abstract/statement level rather than line-by-line full text because its theorem concerns nonexistence of domination rather than eigensections after domination; this comparison does not support any claim about details beyond its stated scope.

value.rationale: The result removes an explicit rank-two limitation from a fresh exact spectral criterion on a natural, structurally stable class: any extremal one-dimensional block of an arbitrary-rank dominated splitting. This is not a parameter substitution; it identifies why the complement dimension is irrelevant, isolates a reusable higher-rank analytic-line extension lemma, and preserves the full sharp Chern/winding dichotomy and exact carried spectrum. The restriction to a one-dimensional extremal block is mathematically natural because the Chern obstruction and scalar multiplier live on that line.
